summary: Sandoval County tower built and staffed by New Mexico State Forestry in 1962; staffed to 1966, demolished in the late 1960s; the history says only foundations remained in 2014.

facts.design: Steel tower with many guy wires and a small plywood cab, as the Santa Fe NF history describes it; no photographs found
facts.status_note: Demolished in the late 1960s per the Santa Fe NF history; the history says only foundations remained in 2014; FFLA lists it as gone
facts.agency: New Mexico State Forestry built and staffed it; the Santa Fe National Forest later funded its staffing

events.note: Built and staffed by State Forestry in 1962; probably completed later that year
Forest inspectors visited in May 1963; no cab on the tower and the lookout unstaffed
A State Fire Control Aid staffed it in 1963 and 1964
Lookout reported fires to the Forest in 1965 and 1966
Frank Gonzales staffed it for State Forestry
Forest felt the structure unsafe and inadequate; a replacement steel tower was proposed but not built
Forest 1968 program of work planned a 54-foot replacement tower; probably derailed when the Accelerated Public Works program ended
History says only foundations remained in 2014

corrections.proposed: New Mexico State Forestry (built and staffed the lookout)
corrections.why: The Santa Fe NF history says State Forestry built and staffed Joaquin in 1962-1966; the Forest only began funding staffing as it acquired grant land in 1964-1965

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1963 Forest inspection found the lookout unstaffed and without a cab, while the same history says a State Fire Control Aid staffed it in 1963 and 1964. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Main source is a detailed Forest history with a full Joaquin section, so built, staffing and fate are well sourced. The history never states the removal year beyond late 1960s, so no removed event is recorded. The concrete footing with a 1962 inscription is described in the history, and the history says only foundations remained in 2014 (the latest site description in the sources read), so whether anything survives today is unknown. The history does not date the Forest's unsafe-structure finding; the 1966 year on that event is the researcher's placement, not a source date. The design paragraph sits in the Joaquin section but the history says no photographs were found, so treat the design line as the history's description. Access is unknown and left out of facts. Record agency Santa Fe National Forest conflicts with the history: State Forestry built and staffed the lookout, see corrections.
